== Problem ==

Let <imath>N</imath> be the product of all the positive integer divisors of <imath>42</imath>. What is the units digit
of <imath>N</imath>?

<imath>\textbf{(A) } 0\qquad\textbf{(B) } 2\qquad\textbf{(C) } 4\qquad\textbf{(D) } 6\qquad\textbf{(E) } 8</imath>

== Solution 1 ==

The factors of <imath>42</imath> are <imath>1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42</imath>. Multiply the unit digits to get <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D) } 6}</imath>

==Solution 2==
The product of the factors of a number <imath>n</imath> is <imath>n^\frac{\tau(n)}{2}</imath>, where <imath>\tau(n)</imath> is the number of positive divisors of <imath>n</imath>. We see that <imath>42 = 2^1 \cdot 3^1 \cdot 7^1</imath> has <imath>(1+1)(1+1)(1+1) = 8</imath> factors, so the product of the divisors of <imath>42</imath> is

<cmath>42^{\frac{8}{2}} \equiv 42^4 \equiv 2^4 \equiv 16 \equiv \boxed{\textbf{(D) } 6} \pmod{10}.</cmath>

==Solution 3==
The factors are <imath>1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42</imath>. We can take out the 1 giving us <imath>2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42</imath>. We can then take the unit digit of each number because the unit digit of the product is dependent on the product of the unit digits in the factors. So the new list is <imath>2, 3, 6, 7, 4, 1, 2</imath>. Taking out the 1 again we get <imath>2, 3, 6, 7, 4, 2</imath>. Multiplying the first 3 numbers gives us <imath>36</imath> which we take the unit digit off. Taking the final 3 digits we get <imath>56</imath> which we take the unit digit off again. This leaves us with 2 numbers which are <imath>6</imath> and <imath>6</imath>, the product of them is 36 and the unit digit of this is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D) } 6}</imath>
